Kevin: FYI — ACME's presales filled the security questionnaire and also asked for a throughput commit estimate for their POC. They want a committed baseline + burst plan. Can SEs advise on sizing and preheat costs?
Maria: TL;DR from customers: steady 250 qps (chat sends) with 20% peak spikes up to 700 qps during business hours. Sequence avg ~120 tokens, 95th token length ~300.
Kevin: They requested reserved GPUs for the commit (prefer predictable latency). Question from procurement: how many r5-style GPUs do we recommend and how does burst billing work?
Raj: For those numbers I'd recommend starting with a reserved pool of 6 A10-like slots (or equivalent throughput units) + burst credit buffer. That gives steady headroom ~300 qps with batching. Burst to 700 qps uses autoscale + prewarm.
Maria: How long to preheat KV/prefix cache to avoid cold-start tail latency? ACME's POC is 10k unique prefixes/day but heavy repeat of top 2k.
Raj: Prefix warm: plan a 90-minute preheat job to populate top-2k prefixes into KV cache. We can script it with the preheat runner. Expect ~5–10% tokens extra for warmup traffic.
Kevin: Procurement wants a cost line item: "preheat compute cost" as a one-time fee for POC. Any ballpark?
Maria: Rough calc: 6 reserved slots * 90 minutes of preheat on dedicated machines. At list reserved-rate, that's ~0.1 of a daily reserved cost. For quoting, say "preheat fee = 6 * 1.5h * hourly-rate" and include a note that we bill actual if preheat > planned.
Lucy: Security notes — ACME's questionnaire: KMS keys must be customer-managed, logs stored for 1 year, and no model weights persist outside GPUs. For Private we can hand off KMS/HSM; for Hosted we support BYOK on enterprise tier.
Kevin: ACME also asked about data residency during POC (EU-only). Can we route presales POC to eu-central region and still keep reserved pool?
Raj: Yes — reserved pools can be AZ/regional. We'll provision a dedicated pool in eu-central and attach autoscale policies same as hosted. Slight startup lead time (~4 business days for Dedicated provisioning).
Maria: Any infra safety nets for burst oversubscribe? They asked about fallback model configs to reduce cost/latency if pool saturation occurs.
Raj: Recommend 2-tier fallback: primary: full model on reserved GPUs. fallback-1: quantized variant (smaller) on same pool for degraded quality but much higher throughput. fallback-2: lower-context model routed to spot capacity (best-effort). We'll configure automatic hedged-routing + rate-limited fallback.
Kevin: Can you paste a sample autoscale snippet we can share in the RFP?
Raj: Sure — share this in thread:
```yaml
autoscale_policy:
  min_replicas: 6
  max_replicas: 12
  target_qps_per_replica: 50
  burst_buffer: 400
  cooldown: 60s
  prewarm: 
    duration: 90m
    runbook: preheat-top-prefixes
```
Maria: Perfect. Also they asked who owns warmup runbooks during POC — us or their SRE?
Raj: We can run the preheat as part of onboarding (one-time), then hand over scripts and runbook. For Dedicated, ops support includes two assisted preheats.
Lucy: Add a security caveat: preheat traffic must be synthetic or scrubbed production data. Document that in the SOW.
Kevin: Procurement wants a single-line estimate for committed monthly cost and a separate line for expected burst billing. Any guidance?
Maria: For a proposal use these items: (1) Reserved capacity monthly: 6 slots * list-monthly (2) Burst credit pool: estimated 10–15% of monthly cost as buffer (3) Preheat fee: one-time as discussed (4) Support: assisted preheat + 2 onboarding calls.
Kevin: Final ask — can someone run a quick rbctl check on eu pool availability so we can give lead time?
capacity-bot: `rbctl capacity list --region eu-central --filter reserved` -> 3 available pre-provisioned slots in vendor pool, dedicated snapshot lead ~4 days.
Raj: I'll open a provisioning ticket with infra and tag @infra on the lead time.
Maria: I'll draft the pricing lines and add the autoscale + fallback config to the RFP. Will ping for approval before sending. :thumbsup:
Kevin: Great — thanks all. I'll include the security note about BYOK and preheat data handling in the questionnaire response and attach Maria's pricing.
Lucy: If ACME asks for SOC/ISO artifacts, I have the packet ready. I'll attach to the thread when we draft the SOW.
Maria: Next step: I'll DM Kevin a compact quote and the draft SOW by EOD.
Kevin: Awesome — closing this thread for now. Will re-open if ACME comes back with follow-ups.
